title: Korea Tourism Organization Act
full_text:
KOREA TOURISM ORGANIZATION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the development of the national economy and the improvement of public welfare by establishing the Korea Tourism Organization and having it conduct projects relating to tourism promotion, development of tourism resources, research and development in the tourism industry, and education and training of tourism-related professionals.

Article 2 (Legal Personality)
The Korea Tourism Organization (hereinafter referred to as the "Organization") shall be a corporation.

Article 3 (Offices)
(1) The location of the principal office of the Organization shall be prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(2) The Organization may establish branches or offices in places where they are needed to perform its duties, subject to a resolution of its board of directors.

Article 4 (Capital)
(1) The capital of the Organization shall be 50 billion won, of which at least one half shall be contributed by the Government.
(2) The Government may make contributions in kind to the Organization of State-owned property, including land, facilities, and goods necessary for the development of tourism businesses.

Article 5 (Registration)
(1) The Organization shall be established upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
(2) Matters necessary for registration of establishment under paragraph (1), registration of the establishment of branches or offices, registration of relocation, registration of changes, and other registrations of the Organization shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Organization may not assert against any third party any matter requiring registration until that matter has been registered. <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>

Article 6 (Prohibition of Use of Similar Names)
No person other than the Organization established under this Act shall use the name "Korea Tourism Organization" or any similar name.

Article 7 (Shares)
(1) The capital of the Organization shall be divided into shares.
(2) Shares shall be registered shares, and their classes and the amount per share shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 8 (Restrictions on Sale of Government-Owned Shares)
Where Government-owned shares are sold to other persons, the total value of shares owned by persons other than the Government shall not exceed the total value of shares owned by the Government.

Article 9 (Restrictions on the President's Power of Representation)
Where the interests of the Organization conflict with those of its President, the President shall not represent the Organization, and the auditor shall represent it instead.

Article 10 (Appointment of Agents)
The President may appoint, from among the employees of the Organization, agents authorized to perform all judicial and extrajudicial acts relating to the affairs of the Organization, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 11 (Prohibition of Disclosure of Confidential Information)
No current or former executive or employee of the Organization shall disclose or misappropriate confidential information learned in the course of performing duties. <Amended on Aug. 8, 2023>

Article 12 (Projects)
(1) The Organization shall conduct the following projects to achieve the purpose prescribed in Article 1: <Amended on Dec. 20, 2016>
1. Projects for the promotion of international tourism:
(a) Publicity to attract foreign tourists;
(b) Research on and development of international tourism markets;
(c) Promotion of international cooperation in tourism;
(d) Guidance and education concerning international tourism;
2. Projects for the promotion of domestic tourism:
(a) Publicity concerning domestic tourism;
(b) Surveys of actual conditions of domestic tourism;
(c) Guidance and education concerning domestic tourism;
(d) Tourism support for groups vulnerable in access to tourism, including persons with disabilities and older persons;
3. Projects for the development of tourism resources:
(a) Creation, management, operation, and disposal of tourist complexes;
(b) Pilot projects for the development of tourism resources and tourism facilities;
(c) Development of tourist destinations;
(d) Surveys of tourism resources;
4. Research and development projects for the tourism industry:
(a) Collection and analysis of information on, and research into, the tourism industry;
(b) Contract research projects relating to research on the tourism industry;
5. Projects for the education and training of tourism-related professionals;
6. Projects resolved upon by the board of directors as incidental projects necessary for the development of tourism businesses, including the import and export of goods.
(2) The Organization may, by resolution of the board of directors, entrust the management of projects under paragraph (1) that it deems necessary to other persons.
(3) The Organization may undertake and implement, upon entrustment from the State, local governments, public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or other public organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree, projects falling under any subparagraph of paragraph (1). <Newly inserted on Dec. 12, 2017>

Article 13 (Disposition of Profits and Losses)
(1) Where the Organization earns a profit upon settlement of accounts for any business year, it shall dispose of the profit in the following order:
1. Coverage of losses carried forward;
2. Appropriation of at least one tenth of the profit to an earned surplus reserve until the reserve reaches one half of the capital;
3. Distribution of dividends to shareholders;
4. Appropriation to reserves other than the earned surplus reserve under subparagraph 2;
5. Carryover to the following year.
(2) Where the Organization incurs a loss upon settlement of accounts for any business year, it shall cover the loss from the reserves under paragraph (1) 4 and, if those reserves are insufficient, from the reserves under paragraph (1) 2; any remaining shortfall shall be carried forward to the following business year.
(3) The reserves under paragraph (1) 2 and 4 may be incorporated into the capital, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Subsidies)
The Government may subsidize the expenses necessary for the projects and operation of the Organization within the budget. <Amended on Dec. 12, 2017>

Article 15 (Issuance of Bonds)
(1) The Organization may issue corporate bonds by resolution of its board of directors, within an amount not exceeding twice the aggregate of its capital and reserves.
(2) The Government may guarantee repayment of the principal and interest on bonds issued by the Organization under paragraph (1).

Article 16 (Supervision)
The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall guide and supervise the affairs of the Organization relating to the following matters, within the scope necessary for the Organization to achieve its management objectives:
1. Projects for the promotion of international and domestic tourism;
2. Projects for the development of tourism resources;
3. Research and development projects for the tourism industry;
4. Projects for the education and training of tourism-related professionals;
5. Projects entrusted to the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism or designated for performance on the Minister's behalf under statutes;
6. Other projects prescribed by relevant statutes.

Article 17 (Relationship to Other Acts)
Matters concerning the organization, management, and other affairs of the Organization not provided for in this Act shall be governed by the Act on the Management of Public Institutions.

Article 18 (Penalty Provisions)
A person who discloses or misappropriates confidential information in violation of Article 11 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Amended on Dec. 12, 2017>

Article 19 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person who uses the name "Korea Tourism Organization" or a similar name in violation of Article 6 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding three million won.
(2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 3845, May 12, 1986>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Act on the Amendment of the Building Act and Other Acts Following Changes in Names of Government Ministries) <Act No. 5454, Dec. 13, 1997>

This Act shall enter into force on January 1, 1998. <Proviso omitted>

ADDENDA (Government Organization Act) <Act No. 8852, Feb. 29, 2008>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That ... <Omitted> ..., the parts amending Acts that were promulgated before the enforcement of this Act but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived, among the Acts amended pursuant to Article 6 of these Addenda, shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Acts.

Articles 2 through 5 Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendments to Other Acts)
(1) through <273> Omitted.
<274> Part of the Korea Tourism Organization Act shall be amended as follows:
In Article 16, "Minister of Culture and Sports" shall be replaced with "Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism."
<275> through <760> Omitted.

Article 7 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Act No. 9474, Mar. 5, 2009>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.
(2) (Transitional Measures concerning Penalty Provisions) The former provisions shall apply when imposing penalties for acts committed before this Act enters into force.

ADDENDA <Act No. 14433, Dec. 20, 2016>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 15171, Dec. 12, 2017>

This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the amended provisions of Article 14 shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

ADDENDA (Act Partially Amending 43 Acts under the Jurisdiction of the Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee for the Improvement of Legal Terminology) <Act No. 19592, Aug. 8, 2023>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
